question: What page load speed should your website achieve to be Black Friday ready?
transcript_excerpt: Your webpage has to load anywhere below two and a half seconds. You should be seeing 2.5 seconds or lower on mobile and desktop versions. Under three seconds is acceptable, but two and a half seconds is the best you can do. Even a fraction of a second delay can hurt your conversion rates and send shoppers to competitors.

question: How do you measure website page speed and performance for SEO?
transcript_excerpt: You can use Google Lighthouse by typing it on Google, or go to pagespeed.web.dev or gtmetrics.com. Once you test your site, you can check what it looks like on mobile and desktop versions. These tools are free and allow you to see your page insights and identify what is slowing down your website performance.

question: What is Flesch Kincaid grade level and why does it matter for website conversions?
transcript_excerpt: Flesch Kincaid grade is a metric that tells your readability level. You want your website content to be at 5th grade level and below, but many sites rank at 12th grade college level which is difficult. If your Flesch reading ease is around 36.5, it means visitors find it hard to read and may take 3 to 9 minutes to understand your content, which negatively impacts conversions.

question: Why does hosting plan bandwidth matter for website performance during high traffic periods?
transcript_excerpt: Your hosting plan bandwidth determines how well your pages load when you have high visitor volume. If you have a million visitors per day and your website crashes because too many people are on the site at the same time, it slows down your site or even breaks it. Big bandwidth allows you to handle big traffic without worrying about site crashes.

question: What are the main factors that slow down website page speed besides internet connection?
transcript_excerpt: What you put in your site determines page load speed more than the user's internet. You could have images that are too large - if you have 50 images at three megabytes each, that is 150 megabytes total when it could be optimized to five megabytes total with each image at 150 kilobytes. You should consider whether you would be happy with your own page load speed before publishing content.
